contracts.operation: LockRect of a sub-rectangle of a render target (backbuffer or lockable render-target surface) whose current copy is its GL texture: read-only and writable, then UnlockRect
contracts.format: X8R8G8B8, A8R8G8B8, X8B8G8R8, A8B8G8R8, R5G6B5, X1R5G5B5, A1R5G5B5, A4R4G4B4, X4R4G4B4
contracts.usage: CPU read/write of part of a render target (UT2003 ReduceMouseLag locks one backbuffer pixel per frame)
contracts.remaining: No frontend or host change. WineD3D downloaded the whole surface (GetTexImage of every texel, 30 synchronous 64 KiB DreamGPU QUERY round trips for 800x600) for any lock that found system memory stale; UT2003's ReduceMouseLag locks one backbuffer pixel read-only after every present (75 FPS with it, 669 without on a Win2000 guest). Wine patch 0056 reads only the locked rectangle with one ReadPixels from a read framebuffer holding the target's texture, into the system-memory copy at the rectangle's offset (pointer and pitch exactly as before), and keeps the texture authoritative: system memory is not marked current, a read-only unlock transfers nothing and a writable unlock uploads only the rectangle (TexSubImage). Full and DISCARD locks, NO_DIRTY_UPDATE writes, a current system-memory copy, depth/stencil, block, converted, color-keyed and other formats, multisampling, the front buffer, targets drawn other than into their texture (ORM_BACKBUFFER, onscreen drawables), DIB/user-memory/PBO/client storage, mipmap levels and cube faces keep the full transfer; an unusable context falls back to it without a transfer. Source tests run the prepared map/unmap state machine against a pixel-tracking GL. The installed D3D8/9 probe (read-only 1x1, 16x16 and last-pixel and writable 8x8 locks of the backbuffer and of lockable X8R8G8B8 and R5G6B5 400x300 render targets, each exact with the whole-lock pitch; only pixels inside each locked rectangle are read) has not yet passed on a guest. Transfer size is measured with transport counters: with 0056's wined3d.dll app-local in UT2003 on Win2000, DM-Antalus with ReduceMouseLag=True ran about 269 FPS (before 67-75) with one ReadPixels QUERY per frame instead of 3 GetTexLevelParameteriv and 30 GetTexImage QUERYs. R5G6B5 targets keep all six green bits with exact RGB565 storage (gl.rgb565-storage, Wine 0057), and the probe then uses all 64 greens; without it Wine stores GL_RGB5 and the probe uses only greens that survive five bits. Win98/XP game runs and macOS CGL remain unverified.

contracts.operation: D3DRS_POINTSPRITEENABLE left set while fixed-function (pretransformed or untransformed) textured triangles and lines draw; point lists with sprites on and off
contracts.format: any texture, one or more coordinate sets
contracts.usage: render to texture, then a pretransformed fixed-function quad copies it to the back buffer (Halo: Combat Evolved PC trial)
contracts.remaining: No frontend or host change. WineD3D enabled GL_POINT_SPRITE whenever the render state was set (COORD_REPLACE is on for every unit), and Mesa 26 (radeonsi and llvmpipe, 26.2.6 on the Linux host) then drops those coordinate sets from fixed-function vertex processing for every primitive, so fixed-function triangles and lines sampled one texel; ARB vertex programs are unaffected. The Halo PC trial sets sprites once and copies its vertex-shader-rendered 800x600 scene texture to the back buffer with one pretransformed indexed fan, so every frame was one colour (also with -useff and before Wine 0049). Wine patch 0058 enables GL_POINT_SPRITE only for point lists and for triangles in point fill mode, re-evaluated on primitive changes to or from points and on fill-mode changes; with sprites off nothing new is sent. Source tests drive the prepared handlers through a model of Wine's invalidation and apply loop. The installed D3D8/9 probe (Halo's 28-byte pretransformed indexed fan, a 16-pixel point and an untransformed strip, sprites on and off, every pixel compared; the sprite itself only when dgpugl.dll reports GL_ARB_point_sprite) has not yet run on a guest, and Halo remains to be rerun. Native OpenGL guests that leave GL_POINT_SPRITE enabled across textured fixed-function triangles still see Mesa's result; Win98/XP and macOS CGL remain unverified.

contracts.operation: IDirect3DDevice8/9::Reset while the device window is minimized or hidden (no client area), repeated, then rendering after restore with and without another reset; WineD3D backup-window fallback
contracts.usage: focus loss and return of a fullscreen game (Warcraft III demo, D3D8)
contracts.remaining: dgpugl.dll refused wglCreateContext on a window without a client area and wglMakeCurrent of a context without a drawable there, or of any context on another such window (ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE for every failure), unlike a native ICD. WineD3D's Reset destroys every GL context before creating the primary one again on the device window, so a Reset while Warcraft III's fullscreen window was still minimized (focus returned without restoring it) failed after the teardown, and its retry dereferenced the NULL context_acquire() result in delete_opengl_contexts (wined3d.dll+0x92BE9 in m41). WineD3D's backup-window fallback (a hidden 10x10 decorated window, empty client area) failed the same way (Halo shutdown logs, last error 0x6). The frontend now accepts any window DC of the process: a context keeps its drawable, whichever window it was made for, while the current window has no client area; a context without one gets a 1x1 placeholder that the first window with a client area (MakeCurrent or SwapBuffers) replaces; nothing is presented meanwhile; presentation capabilities come from the last binding. Wine patch 0059 makes the reset fail cleanly (D3DERR_DEVICELOST, nothing changed) when its context cannot be made current, keeps a device whose primary context could not be created again lost without any context (no bare context is created; the retry creates it, no double free of shader/blitter state or the context array) and lets reset teardown, uninit, end-scene, clear, draw, present and surface/buffer/volume/texture unloads run without a context. Source tests execute the prepared functions and the frontend. The installed D3D8/9 probe (visible, minimized twice, restored without reset, hidden/shown and final resets, 4 exact reference frames) has not yet run on a guest; Warcraft III's focus loss and return remain to be rerun on Win2000. Fullscreen mode handoff during these resets is unchanged (0025); Win98/XP and macOS CGL remain unverified.

contracts.api: D3D8/D3D9 fullscreen swapchain (WineD3D device window) over WGL (dgpugl.dll)
contracts.operation: focus loss and activation of a fullscreen device (WM_ACTIVATEAPP) with the device window minimized by WineD3D; the application's own SetWindowPos/MoveWindow of the fullscreen device window, including nested in WineD3D's SetWindowPos from WM_SIZE; Reset to the same mode, another mode and windowed
contracts.usage: fullscreen game whose window was created smaller than its mode and that sizes it back (Splinter Cell, D3D8, 1024x768 on a 640x480 window)
contracts.remaining: Native fullscreen flips cover the screen whatever the device window's size; DreamGPU presents into the window's client area (WineD3D's GetClientRect destination, the display drivers' WNDOBJ client rectangle). Splinter Cell sizes its fullscreen window back to its 640x480 creation size from WM_SIZE, nested in WineD3D's own SetWindowPos, so it showed in a corner of the 1024x768 mode; after a focus change WineD3D's activation kept the window it had minimized iconic (wined3d sees only sent messages, and the taskbar's SC_RESTORE is posted), and the game never reset. Wine patch 0060 restores the iconic device window on activation (SW_SHOWNOACTIVATE) and, while a D3D8/9 swapchain is fullscreen and the application active, subclasses the device window (A/W functions matching IsWindowUnicode) and clamps its WM_WINDOWPOSCHANGING to 0,0 and the mode size when a request would leave part of the mode uncovered, before and after the application's procedure (at most 8 clamps between presents); minimizing, restoring, pure moves, DirectDraw and NOWINDOWCHANGES devices are unchanged, and Reset updates the kept size before its mode change. The first 0060 clamped in WineD3D's WH_CALLWNDPROC hook; on Windows 2000 (m43 installer probe) the window stayed 320x240, since hooks get a copy. The subclass is removed when keeping stops, left as a pass-through when another module subclassed later, and forgotten on WM_NCDESTROY. Source tests run the prepared functions against a user32 model that discards hook-time edits and models the procedure chain. WineD3D's activation hack passed sizeof(struct wined3d_device) (about 50 KiB) as VirtualQuery's buffer length; Windows validates that length, which ran past a shallow stack's base, so focus loss and activation were ignored on Windows XP and 98 (m44 probe: window not minimized); 0060 passes sizeof(meminfo), and the clamp also skips requests to the parked minimized position (Windows 98 has no SWP_STATECHANGED). Source tests model Windows 2000/XP, 98 (no SWP_STATECHANGED, on-screen minimized position) and late-iconic variants. The installed D3D8/9 probe (reset-probe.inc Fullscreen, run last) passes on Windows 2000 (m44) and remains to be rerun on XP and 98; Splinter Cell remains to be run.

contracts.api: IDirect3DDevice8/9 SetCursorProperties, SetCursorPosition and ShowCursor (WineD3D) over WGL (dgpugl.dll) and the display drivers' native cursor
contracts.operation: show, move and hide a Direct3D cursor on a fullscreen device: a 32x32 image as a Windows cursor (SetCursorPos), any other size, or a 32x32 one the Windows cursor cannot follow, drawn by WineD3D into the back buffer at Present with an alpha-tested blit
contracts.format: A8R8G8B8 cursor image; X8R8G8B8 or R5G6B5 back buffer
contracts.resource: cursor image surface and swapchain back buffer
contracts.usage: game menus that use the Direct3D cursor
contracts.pool: system memory image; default pool cursor texture
contracts.remaining: The installed D3D8/9 probe (cursor-probe.inc, run last on its own fullscreen 640x480 device) reads the presented frame back with GetFrontBuffer/GetFrontBufferData and checks a 16x16 cursor drawn by WineD3D at two positions (alpha-tested transparent half absent, old position clear, hidden after ShowCursor(FALSE)), a 32x32 Windows cursor shown and positioned (GetCursorInfo, frame clear) at two positions, a 32x32 cursor drawn by WineD3D once ClipCursor keeps SetCursorPos from reaching it, and a 16x16 cursor across the bottom-right and (hotspot 8,8) top-left corners, each with nothing else in the frame; it has not run on a guest. WineD3D (wine9x swapchain.c) passed the unclipped cursor rectangle to wined3d_surface_blt, which rejects any destination outside the back buffer (WINEDDERR_INVALIDRECT), so a cursor drawn by WineD3D vanished while any part of it was beyond an edge; Wine patch 0061 clips the destination to the back buffer and the source by the same amounts, as native Direct3D and later Wine (wined3d_clip_blit) do, with signed edges for a hotspot beyond the position. Source tests run the prepared cursor block and clip helper with the prepared blit validation (every pixel compared, 13 mutations rejected). The fixed-function blitter's alpha-tested blit (no ARB_fragment_program) disables the alpha test it enables, so transparent texels would be drawn; DreamGPU's arbfp blitter is used where ARB_fragment_program is advertised. Battlefield 1942 and Painkiller draw their own menu cursor sprites at positions accumulated from DirectInput deltas and clamped to the screen (their executables: BF1942's textured cursor quad, Painkiller's PainMenu::SetMouseTexture and DIInputSystem clamp), so their vanishing menu cursors are an input-delta problem, not this interface.

Prepared source verifies windowed activation leaves global mode alone, explicit same-mode fullscreen requests reach the native ownership call, fullscreen Alt+Tab and mode-setting failures preserve state. Prepared-source checks cover GDI completion, primary read/write preservation, and persistent primary loss/restoration across exclusive focus and mode changes. Installed Win2000 Golf 1999 Quick Start/menus pass; its modal+Alt+Tab artifacts (black terrain until the modal closes, blank YES/NO, missing toolbar half) are identical on Microsoft DirectDraw and on stock Cirrus + Microsoft DirectDraw, so they are game behavior, not a DreamGPU defect. 8-bit (P8) primaries with a GL swapchain are excluded from the desktop readback (Wine 0067): the device writes publications back only into 16/32-bit scanout, so every Lock replaced the application's indices with stale desktop pixels (StarCraft's once-drawn in-mission console was one flat colour; a guest probe read index 0 for all 307,200 pixels it had drawn). The primary's own storage is authoritative and each publication copies all of it; StarCraft's console renders on Windows 98 (m54 + 0067). GDI drawing onto an 8-bit swapchain desktop is not merged into the primary. Broader installed GDI/GPU ordering remains unverified.

contracts.operation: IsEnabled and GetBooleanv/GetIntegerv/GetFloatv/GetDoublev of the tracked capabilities and VIEWPORT answered from the context's state shadow
contracts.remaining: Known values: GL defaults at creation (every tracked capability disabled except DITHER) and setters executed outside display lists; the viewport only after an unclamped Viewport. contracts.operation: pretransformed (XYZRHW) vertex fog from specular alpha, applied after texturing
contracts.remaining: Negotiated by DG_CAP_GL_FOG_COORD (FogCoordf, FOG_COORDINATE_SOURCE, DrawArraysEXT slot 14). Wine previously emulated it by blending vertex colours before texturing, which darkens textured geometry instead of fogging it; the installed textured probe fails on that build and passes on Win2000 and XP. The Wine fast path packs specular-alpha fog coordinates. Wine patch 0041 gives fixed-function array draws (buffer objects) a float fog coordinate array with drawStridedSlow's values instead of emulating them in immediate mode; D3DCOLOR streams outside buffer objects stay in immediate mode without BGRA vertex arrays (with DG_CAP_GL_VERTEX_ARRAY_BGRA they take the fog coordinate array too). The installed D3D7 probe and D3D8/9 vertex buffer probe add exact untransformed buffer and UP fog quads, untested on guests. Table fog, range fog, vertex-processed fog modes, macOS CGL and Win98 remain unverified.

contracts.api: D3D8/D3D9 vertex shaders (WineD3D ARB backend, arbfp fragment pipe) with D3DRS_FOGTABLEMODE LINEAR/EXP/EXP2
contracts.operation: table fog of draws whose vs_1_x/vs_2_x shader writes oFog: the oFog value through the table equation with FOGSTART/FOGEND/FOGDENSITY, as NVIDIA (before 61.77) and ATI drivers of 2003-2004 did
contracts.remaining: WineD3D wrote the vertex output z as the fog coordinate under table fog, as the reference rasterizer and later drivers do; Far Cry's NVIDIA path (DreamGPU reports a GeForce FX) writes oFog with FOGTABLEMODE LINEAR, start 0 and end 1 and relies on the period drivers' use of oFog, so its terrain, water and boat were drawn in the fog colour (Wine bug 25761; Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time, bug 17423, does the same). Wine patch 0062 passes the oFog of vs_1_x/vs_2_x shaders with built-in varyings to result.fogcoord unclamped (whether the period drivers clamped it is undocumented; Wine's proof-of-concept fix left it unclamped); vertex fog keeps the clamped oFog factor, and vs_3_0, declared varyings and shaders without oFog keep the vertex output z. Known divergence, unchanged: without oFog native table fog uses W under a perspective D3DTS_PROJECTION and z/w (AMD) or the vertex output z (NVIDIA) under an orthographic one; WineD3D always uses the vertex output z. Source tests interpret the prepared epilogue with the prepared fog source selection (7 mutations rejected). The installed D3D8/9 probe (table-fog-probe.inc: oFog 0, 1, 0.25 under LINEAR 0..1, oFog 2 under 0..4, vertex fog oFog 1 and 0, fixed-function and ps_1_1 fragments) has not run on a guest; Far Cry and Prince of Persia remain to be run. The GLSL backend is never selected (no ARB_fragment_shader/ARB_vertex_shader) and is unchanged.

contracts.api: D3D8/D3D9 vertex shaders (WineD3D ARB backend) into fixed-function texture stages (arbfp fragment pipe) sampling conditional NPOT textures
contracts.operation: fixed-function texture lookups of a rectangle (or padded NPOT 2D) texture with the normalized coordinates a vertex shader writes: scaled by the texture's pow2_matrix in the fragment program, as the texture matrix does for fixed-function vertices
contracts.format: any rectangle-capable colour format, NPOT render-target textures included
contracts.remaining: Without ARB_texture_non_power_of_two WineD3D (GeForce FX quirk) creates NPOT textures, such as an 800x600 render-target texture, as rectangles, which take texel coordinates; get_texture_matrix() multiplies the application's normalized coordinates by the texture's pow2_matrix, but transform_texture() skips the texture matrix under a vertex shader. Thief: Deadly Shadows renders its scene into an 800x600 render-target texture and draws it to the back buffer with a vertex shader and fixed-function stage 0, so every pixel showed texel (0, 0) of the scene: a uniform near-black screen with only the HUD drawn after it (host trace: fixed-function program 40 sampling RECT texture 41 with no coordinate scale). Wine patch 0064 keys a fixed-function stage vs_np2_fixup exactly when the texture matrix would have scaled but is skipped (a vertex shader and a texture without WINED3D_TEXTURE_POW2_MAT_IDENT) and multiplies the coordinate by program.local[stage] = (pow2 width, pow2 height, 1, 1) before plain, projected (count3/count4) and bump-mapped lookups; the locals load when the program is bound and on sampler() reloads for another NPOT texture. A host Mesa replay of the generated programs on an 800x600 rectangle gives one colour before and the scene after. Source tests interpret the prepared programs and loader (10 mutations rejected). The installed D3D8/9 NPOT probe draws the 640x480 texture's quarters through vs_1_1 into stage 0 and requires every texel; it passes on Windows 2000, XP and Windows 98 (m53), and Thief: Deadly Shadows renders its world in gameplay on Windows 2000 (about 103 FPS on m53, 114 with 0065). Pixel shaders keep Wine's np2fixup; point sprites with rectangles are unchanged.

contracts.api: D3D8/D3D9 vertex and index buffers (WineD3D buffer objects over DreamGPU ARB_vertex_buffer_object)
contracts.operation: creating a buffer object (glGenBuffers, glBindBuffer, glBufferData) without glGetError queries, so mid-frame buffer creation does not wait for the host to drain the stream
contracts.remaining: A DreamGPU glGetError is a synchronous query that the host answers only after executing everything queued before it. WineD3D brackets every buffer object creation with four of them (an error-clearing loop and checks after glGenBuffers, glBindBuffer and glBufferData); Thief: Deadly Shadows creates an 84-byte vertex buffer and a 6-byte index buffer each frame after its scene (host trace: 8 glGetError queries per frame), so the guest waited for the host to finish the frame so far once per frame. Wine patch 0065 drops the queries: names and bindings are guest-local in DreamGPU, so a zero name is the only synchronous failure, and a host GL_OUT_OF_MEMORY from glBufferData stays pending as on a native driver instead of steering WineD3D to its non-VBO fallback. Thief: Deadly Shadows gameplay on Windows 2000 went from about 103 to 114 FPS (42 instead of 54 transport batches per frame). Startup format probing still queries errors.

contracts.api: DirectDraw EnumDisplayModes / D3D adapter mode enumeration (WineD3D) for 8-bit palettized formats
contracts.operation: enumerating P8 display modes: the 32-bit desktop modes that a P8 SetDisplayMode actually sets (8-bit desktops are emulated on 32 bpp)
contracts.remaining: WineD3D never sets an 8-bit desktop mode: a P8 request switches to 32 bits per pixel and converts the palette on presentation. Mode enumeration still matched the 8-bit format against the driver list, and the Windows 2000/XP display driver lists only 16- and 32-bit modes, so DirectDraw reported no 8-bit mode while SetDisplayMode(w, h, 8) worked. Age of Empires II looks for its 8-bit mode first and stopped with "Could not initialize graphics system". Wine patch 0068 enumerates P8 modes from the 32-bit modes the setter uses (also on Windows 98, where the same resolutions result); 16-bit and d3d8 (UNKNOWN) enumeration are unchanged. With an app-local 0068 wined3d.dll Age of Empires II reaches its 800x600 8-bit main menu on Windows XP with correct colours.

contracts.operation: non-indexed vertex blending (D3DRS_VERTEXBLEND 1-3 weights, WORLD..WORLD3) of positions and normals; MaxVertexBlendMatrices/MaxVertexBlendMatrixIndex
contracts.format: FLOAT1-4 or D3DCOLOR blend weights, FLOAT3/4 positions, FLOAT3/4 normals
contracts.remaining: No capability bit and no frontend or host change: GL_ARB_vertex_blend stays unadvertised (Mesa lacks it and a GeForce FX never listed it), and Wine patch 0052 blends on the CPU instead. WineD3D now reports the GeForce FX's MaxVertexBlendMatrices 4 and MaxVertexBlendMatrixIndex 0 (D3D8 and D3D9; before 1 and 0) and draws D3DRS_VERTEXBLEND 1-3 weights: each vertex's position and normal blended into world space (sum of w_i v WORLDi, normals through each WORLDi inverse transpose, the last weight 1 minus the others) as client arrays of an array draw, or per vertex in immediate mode, under the view matrix alone, so lights, clip planes, texture generation and fog keep eye space. Other draws, including 0 weights (indexed blending, not claimed), weights without blending and unreadable streams, are unchanged; tweening is d3d.vertex-tween (Wine 0053, same helpers). VertexProcessingCaps stay D3D9 0x13b and D3D8 0x13f under 0052; 0053 adds the FX's D3DVTXPCAPS_TWEENING. Source tests run the prepared helpers against an eye-space ARB_vertex_blend reference; native pixel tests (Linux) draw the frontend's records of such draws with lighting, fog and a clip plane under the view. The installed D3D8/9 probe (two-, three- and four-matrix quads from user memory and indexed buffers, lit normals with and without NORMALIZENORMALS), D3D7, macOS CGL, Win98/XP guests and games remain to be run.

contracts.operation: vertex tweening (D3DRS_VERTEXBLEND D3DVBF_TWEENING, D3DRS_TWEENFACTOR) of positions and normals from D3D9 POSITION1/NORMAL1 or D3D8 D3DVSDE_POSITION2/NORMAL2; D3DVTXPCAPS_TWEENING
contracts.format: FLOAT3/4 positions and normals, second elements in any stream
contracts.remaining: No capability bit and no frontend or host change. WineD3D never tweened: it printed a FIXME, had no fixed-function slot for the second position and normal and drew the first. Wine patch 0053 tweens on the CPU with 0052's helpers: POSITION1 * (1 - TWEENFACTOR) + POSITION2 * TWEENFACTOR (as Direct3D documents it; normals likewise) in object space, each second element read from its stream's system memory copy, drawn as 0052's client arrays or immediate-mode Normal3fv/Vertex4fv under Wine's own modelview, so the GL records are 0052's without its matrix calls (native-vertex-blend draws that shape). D3D9 VertexProcessingCaps become the GeForce FX's 0x17b (before 0x13b), D3D8 0x17f (before 0x13f); D3D7 has no tweening. Vertex shaders, pretransformed positions, other formats, per-instance data and unreadable second streams keep the untweened draw; draws without tweening are unchanged. Source tests run the prepared helpers against a double-precision reference of the documented formula. The installed D3D8/9 probe (positions from user memory, a vertex buffer and two indexed streams at factors 0, 1/2 and 1, a stretched quad, lit normals with and without NORMALIZENORMALS), macOS CGL, Win98/XP guests and games remain to be run.

contracts.api: D3D8 (d3d8.dll exports through the switcher to Wine)
contracts.operation: ValidatePixelShader(code, caps, return_error, errors) and ValidateVertexShader(code, declaration, caps, return_error, errors), as D3DX8 calls them after assembling a shader
contracts.usage: statically linked D3DX8 (D3DXAssembleShader) in games and benchmarks
contracts.remaining: Wine patch 0054 is upstream Wine's implementation: version token checked, against the caps when given, a process-heap error string (empty unless return_error is set) when errors is given; the stubs failed with any caps or declaration and never wrote the string. D3DX8 as linked into UT2003's D3DDrv.dll and 3DMark2001 SE passes NULL caps and declaration and a NULL-initialized string and frees it with HeapFree(GetProcessHeap()). Its D3DXERR_INVALIDDATA came from the d3d8 switcher: with unkToSystemDll (0003) only Direct3DCreate8 reached Wine and both validators hit the system list's E_FAIL stubs on images without msd3d8.dll; patch 0055 routes every export Wine implements to Wine (d3d8, d3d9 and ddraw reviewed), fixes D3D8GetSWInfo's stub arity and makes the pointer and query stubs safe. UT2003's DM-Antalus terrain rendered on Win2000 with wined8.dll application-local; the installed D3D8 probes (DGD3D8 through wined8.dll, DGSYS8 through the switcher), UT2003 and 3DMark2001 through the switcher remain to be run.

contracts.remaining: Negotiated by DG_CAP_GL_TEXTURE_CUBE_MAP. The installed D3D8/9 probe samples a MANAGED A8R8G8B8 cube texture's six faces exactly on Win2000, XP and Win98 SE (Linux host). Cube mip chains, compressed cube faces through D3D, render-to-cube-face, seamless/edge filtering, macOS CGL and the macOS border sampler for cube targets remain unverified.

contracts.api: OpenGL 1.1 + ARB_fragment_program (D3D8/D3D9 pixel shaders 1.x-2.0, the ARB fixed-function fragment pipeline and arbfp blitter through Wine)
contracts.operation: program objects and namespaces, ProgramString with error position/string, env/local parameters, FRAGMENT_PROGRAM_ARB enable, program matrices, program and limit queries, display lists, ENABLE_BIT
contracts.format: ARBfp1.0 ASCII program strings up to DG_GL_MAX_PROGRAM_BYTES
contracts.remaining: Negotiated by DG_CAP_GL_FRAGMENT_PROGRAM; vertex programs are the separate gl.vertex-program contract. On Linux the private Mesa provider rejects drawing with GL_INVALID_OPERATION while a program samples a texture with supplied borders; on macOS the border sampler steps aside and CGL ignores the borders. Wine patch 0029 adapts paletted textures, colour keys, the fixed-function program grammar, NP2 fixups, vertex-shader guards and depth uploads; 0030 keeps constants set between draws (no current context after 0012); 0031 declares the fixed-function generator's sign-fixup temporary. The installed D3D8/9 shader probe (ps_1_1, ps_2_0 on D3D9, D3DTOP_BUMPENVMAP from V8U8) passes on Win2000, XP and Win98 SE (Linux host) with PixelShaderVersion 2.0 (D3D8 1.4). Shader-model ps_1_2-1_4 instructions, texbem/texbeml in shaders, ps_2_0 flow limits, macOS CGL and games using pixel shaders remain unverified.

contracts.api: OpenGL 1.1 + ARB_vertex_program (D3D8/D3D9 vertex shaders 1.1-2.0 through Wine's ARB backend)
contracts.operation: VERTEX_PROGRAM_ARB objects in the shared program namespace, ProgramString with error position/string, env/local parameters, VERTEX_PROGRAM_ARB/POINT_SIZE/TWO_SIDE enables, generic attributes (VertexAttrib*ARB outside and inside Begin/End and in display lists, client arrays through the attribute draw), attribute 0 aliasing the position, program/attribute/limit queries, ENABLE_BIT/CURRENT_BIT/CLIENT_VERTEX_ARRAY_BIT
contracts.format: ARBvp1.0 ASCII program strings up to DG_GL_MAX_PROGRAM_BYTES; 16 generic attributes of every GL 1.1 component type, sizes 1-4, normalized or not
contracts.remaining: Negotiated by DG_CAP_GL_VERTEX_PROGRAM; without it the extension and entry points are hidden and vertex program modes stay GL_INVALID_ENUM. Generic client arrays travel in their own DATA record (the VertexAttribPointerARB function number, 16 conventional and 16 generic descriptors), so older kernels keep their DrawArrays/DrawArraysEXT admission. Attribute 0 is the position (the non-aliasing GL 2.0 model Mesa implements): its array supersedes the vertex array and generic attributes 1-15 never alias conventional ones. Host checks reject non-ASCII bytes and vertex.attrib[n] at or beyond MAX_VERTEX_ATTRIBS_ARB (16); other semantic limits are native. Every vertex load goes into a fresh native object that replaces the program's on success (Mesa 26.1 frees a serialized program twice when one vertex object is translated three times). Native pixel tests (Linux, private Mesa on Radeon) cover env-parameter transforms, every generic array type and size, current values inside and outside Begin/End, position aliasing, program matrices and state.matrix.mvp, per-vertex point size, two-sided colours, relative addressing, parse and host-detected failures, invalid-program draws, display lists, ENABLE_BIT/CURRENT_BIT, combined vertex and fragment programs, sharing/isolation, and the vs_1_1/vs_2_0 programs WineD3D generates for the installed probe. Wine patch 0033 maps glVertexAttrib2svARB, clamps VS 2.0 NumTemps, sets VERTEX_PROGRAM_POINT_SIZE only for oPts writers, disables vertex programs for CPU depth uploads and binds the zero attribute as a client array without ARB_vertex_buffer_object. Expected caps: D3D9 VertexShaderVersion 2.0 with 256 constants, D3D8 1.1. VS 2.0 makes Wine report its NVIDIA fallback for that level, a GeForce FX 5800 (10de:0302, previously a GeForce 256), whose quirk enabled the rectangle textures DreamGPU lacks and blacked out DirectDraw/D3D6/D3D7 presentation until patch 0034. The installed D3D8/9 vertex shader probe (vs_1_1 for two constant sets, vs_2_0 on D3D9, vs_1_1 into ps_1_1) passes on Win2000, XP and Win98 SE (Linux host). Signed normalized generic arrays convert natively (c/32767) while immediate and ArrayElement 4N values follow GL 1.x; D3D point size limits, ARB_vertex_buffer_object, macOS CGL and games using vertex shaders remain unverified.

contracts.api: OpenGL 1.1 + EXT_texture3D (D3D8/D3D9 volume textures through Wine)
contracts.operation: TEXTURE_3D definition/subimage/copy/readback, zero-defined storage, proxies, mip levels, per-unit binding with TEXTURE_BIT, TEXTURE_WRAP_R, IMAGE_HEIGHT/SKIP_IMAGES pixel storage
contracts.format: uncompressed internal formats; every 2D wire format and GL 1.2 packed type
contracts.remaining: Negotiated by DG_CAP_GL_TEXTURE_3D; without it the extension, entry points, enums and image pixel storage stay hidden. TexImage3D/TexSubImage3D are nine- and ten-word DATA records with tight payloads (the frontend resolves every unpack value and splits into bounded slabs of whole images or 2D tiles); CopyTexSubImage3D is a nine-word CALL. MAX_3D_TEXTURE_SIZE is 256; images are borderless (a border is GL_INVALID_OPERATION, its proxy rejected) and compressed 3D formats are not accepted. Native pixel tests (Linux, private Mesa on Radeon) sample slices at explicit R with NEAREST and LINEAR filtering, mip levels, WRAP_R, subimages, copies, readback through every image, zero definitions, tight RGB and packed payloads, proxies, display lists, per-unit bindings and TEXTURE_BIT, 3D over 2D precedence and the incomplete fallback. Wine claims VOLUMEMAP, MIPVOLUMEMAP and VOLUMEMAP_POW2; patch 0035 states the unpack alignment of volume uploads. The installed D3D8/9 volume probe (four LockBox slices of a MANAGED A8R8G8B8 4x4x4 texture) is untested on guests; DEFAULT-pool LockBox, volume mip chains through D3D, converted formats, shaders sampling volumes, macOS CGL and games remain unverified.

contracts.api: OpenGL 1.1 + ARB_vertex_buffer_object (D3D8/D3D9 vertex and index buffers through Wine)
contracts.operation: ARRAY_BUFFER/ELEMENT_ARRAY_BUFFER objects in the shared namespace: Gen/Delete/Is/Bind, BufferData (all usage hints), BufferSubData, GetBufferSubData, Map/Unmap, GetBufferParameteriv/Pointerv; array pointers latching buffer offsets (conventional, units 1-7, fog, generic attributes, InterleavedArrays), *_ARRAY_BUFFER_BINDING queries, DrawArrays/DrawElements from buffers, ArrayElement, display list dereference
contracts.remaining: Negotiated by DG_CAP_GL_VERTEX_BUFFER_OBJECT; without it the extension and entry points are hidden and every draw is unchanged. BufferData/BufferSubData/DeleteBuffers name their buffer and execute immediately (never compiled); contents up to DG_GL_MAX_BUFFER_BYTES travel in bounded BufferSubData slabs and are charged against the resource budget. Bindings, array latches and mappings are frontend client state; the frontend keeps a copy of every buffer, so maps return it (16-byte aligned), Unmap re-sends it unless READ_ONLY, and reads never wait for the host. Draws reading buffers use the buffer draw (DATA function DrawRangeElements: references per slot, client sections of the indexed vertex range, inline or element-buffer indices), so older kernels keep every existing admission; the host bounds every read against current sizes, scanning element-buffer indices in its own copy, and state-dependent failures are GL errors. Display list compilation and anything the record cannot express (unaligned offsets, strides beyond 2048, oversized client sections) dereference the buffers into client draws. BufferData on a mapped buffer unmaps it, as in Mesa; buffers deleted in another context end its draws with GL_INVALID_OPERATION. Wine patches 0037-0040 double-buffer buffer objects with dirty-range BufferSubData uploads, repair this tree's fixed-function D3DCOLOR/XYZRHW conversion, keep immediate mode on memory and size/delete the zero attribute buffer; dynamic buffers stay in system memory without ARB_map_buffer_range. Native pixel tests, the installed D3D8/9 vertex buffer probe, macOS CGL and games remain to be run on guests.

contracts.api: OpenGL 1.1 + EXT_framebuffer_object, EXT_framebuffer_blit, EXT_packed_depth_stencil (D3D8/D3D9 render targets through Wine ORM_FBO)
contracts.operation: framebuffer objects per context and renderbuffers in the shared namespace: Gen/Delete/Is/Bind (FRAMEBUFFER, DRAW/READ_FRAMEBUFFER), RenderbufferStorage, FramebufferTexture1D/2D/3D (cube faces, 3D slices), FramebufferRenderbuffer, CheckFramebufferStatus, GetFramebufferAttachmentParameteriv, GetRenderbufferParameteriv, GenerateMipmap, BlitFramebuffer, per-framebuffer draw/read buffers, binding queries, ReadPixels/CopyTex*/CopyPixels from objects, 2D depth and packed depth/stencil textures
contracts.format: RGB/RGBA sized colour, DEPTH_COMPONENT16/24/32, STENCIL_INDEX1-16, DEPTH24_STENCIL8
contracts.usage: render target, depth-stencil and blit source/destination
contracts.remaining: Negotiated by DG_CAP_GL_FRAMEBUFFER_OBJECT; without it the extensions, entry points and enums stay hidden. Framebuffer names are virtual and per context; zero stays the host's drawable framebuffer, rebound by the host under the guest's objects on every make-current, exchange and export, so presentation and window readback are unchanged with an object bound. Every command but BlitFramebuffer executes immediately; state-dependent failures are GL errors and completeness is the native GL 3 rules (no INCOMPLETE_DIMENSIONS/FORMATS). Attachments keep deleted images alive until detached; rendering into them is fenced for other contexts and versioned for the texture read cache. Renderbuffers are zero-initialized and charged against the resource budget; reads of uninitialized images are INVALID_FRAMEBUFFER_OPERATION; ReadPixels from an object is clipped by the host to its attachments. 2D textures take depth and packed depth/stencil formats for depth attachments; ARB_depth_texture and depth GetTexImage are not claimed. Wine selects ORM_FBO, and with this tree's always_offscreen every D3D8/9 swapchain renders into an FBO and presents with glBlitFramebuffer; patches 0042-0046 keep NPOT resources in padded 2D textures, give CPU depth transfers an FBO mode, attach larger depth buffers directly, send overlapping self-blits to the CPU blitter and keep point sprites upright through POINT_SPRITE_COORD_ORIGIN below GL 2.0. Native pixel tests pass on Linux; the installed D3D8/9 render-target probe, the existing probes under ORM_FBO, adapter-start format checks (R5G6B5 targets, blending), macOS CGL, Win98/XP guests and games remain to be run.

contracts.api: OpenGL 1.1 + ARB_vertex_array_bgra (D3DCOLOR vertex streams through Wine)
contracts.operation: size BGRA for ColorPointer, SecondaryColorPointerEXT and VertexAttribPointerARB (normalized); its errors; BGRA size queries and CLIENT_VERTEX_ARRAY_BIT; client-memory, buffer-object, display list and ArrayElement draws
contracts.usage: diffuse, specular and generic vertex attributes
contracts.remaining: Negotiated by DG_CAP_GL_VERTEX_ARRAY_BGRA; without it BGRA stays an invalid size and every draw is unchanged. The frontend reorders client memory into the RGBA sections of the existing array records (a secondary colour as RGB), so older records, kernels and hosts keep their admission; a draw with a BGRA buffer slot uses the BGRA buffer draw (DATA function DrawRangeElementsEXT: the buffer draw plus DG_GL_ARRAY_BGRA on colour, secondary colour and generic buffer slots), which the NT/Win9x kernels and the host check like the buffer draw and which native GL reads with size BGRA. Lists and the record's fallbacks dereference buffers into reordered client draws. Wine then draws fixed-function D3DCOLOR diffuse/specular streams outside buffer objects (D3D8/9 UP, dynamic and SYSTEMMEM buffers, D3D5-7 user memory and system-memory vertex buffers) from arrays instead of immediate mode, stops converting D3DCOLOR in buffer objects, and feeds vertex shaders GL_BGRA generic arrays; Wine 0048 draws XYZRHW streams outside buffer objects from arrays too (positions converted as immediate mode converted them, colours in place as GL_BGRA). Wine 0047 fixes the stride-zero D3DCOLOR zero attribute. Native pixel tests pass on Linux; the installed D3D7 and D3D8/9 colour-array and XYZRHW probes, macOS CGL (EXT_vertex_array_bgra), Win98/XP guests and game performance remain to be run.

contracts.api: OpenGL 1.1 + ARB_occlusion_query and NV_fence (D3D9 occlusion and event queries through Wine)
contracts.operation: Gen/Delete/Is/Begin/EndQuery, GetQueryiv (CURRENT_QUERY, QUERY_COUNTER_BITS), GetQueryObject(u)iv (RESULT, RESULT_AVAILABLE) and their errors; Gen/Delete/Set/Test/Finish/IsFenceNV and GetFenceivNV; display lists
contracts.remaining: Negotiated by DG_CAP_GL_OCCLUSION_QUERY; without it the extensions and entry points stay hidden and every entry point fails locally. Query and fence objects belong to one context and the host owns names, objects and the active query; BeginQuery, EndQuery and SetFenceNV compile into display lists, deletion executes immediately, and every state-dependent failure (nesting, Gen/Delete while active, results of non-objects or the active query) is a GL error. Results stay asynchronous on the host: a pending availability or fence status flushes native GL, QUERY_RESULT and FinishFenceNV wait, and one GetQueryObject round trip carries the result and the results of earlier ended queries, which the frontend keeps with signalled fences until the name is begun, set or deleted or a list executes. Objects are charged against the resource budget, at most 4096 names per kind and context. Wine then creates D3DQUERYTYPE_OCCLUSION queries (D3DERR_NOTAVAILABLE before) and backs D3DQUERYTYPE_EVENT with NV fences (an issued event's GetData failed with D3DERR_INVALIDCALL before); this Wine still answers a pending event S_OK with FALSE. Native pixel tests pass on Linux; the installed D3D9 query probe, macOS CGL, Win98/XP guests and games remain to be run.

contracts.api: OpenGL 1.1 + ARB_texture_rectangle and NV_texture_rectangle (D3D8/D3D9 conditional non-power-of-two textures through Wine)
contracts.operation: TEXTURE_RECTANGLE definition/subimage/copy/readback, zero-defined storage, proxies, per-unit binding and enable with TEXTURE_BIT, parameters and their errors, framebuffer attachment, ARB_fragment_program RECT sampling, display lists
contracts.format: uncompressed colour internal formats of any size up to 2048, level zero, no border; every 2D wire format and GL 1.2 packed type
contracts.usage: sampling and rendering with unnormalized coordinates
contracts.remaining: Negotiated by DG_CAP_GL_TEXTURE_RECTANGLE; without it the extension names stay hidden and every rectangle enum keeps its GL_INVALID_ENUM. No new records: the 2D image, copy, readback, level query and FramebufferTexture2D records name TEXTURE_RECTANGLE (and its proxy), with level zero, no border, no compressed or depth format and at most 2048 per side as record rules the frontend checks locally; parameter values (REPEAT, MIRRORED_REPEAT and mirror-once wraps, mipmap filters, a nonzero BASE_LEVEL) are native GL errors and GENERATE_MIPMAP is no rectangle parameter. ARB_texture_non_power_of_two is not claimed (GL_VERSION stays 1.1), so 2D textures stay power-of-two for WineD3D. Native pixel tests (Linux, private Mesa) sample a 37x23 rectangle exactly with NEAREST and LINEAR including its last row and column and CLAMP_TO_EDGE beyond them, and cover subimages, CopyTexImage2D/CopyTexSubImage2D, readback, proxies, the spec's errors, rendering into a rectangle through a framebuffer object, ARB fragment program TEX/TXP with RECT, enable precedence, per-unit bindings with TEXTURE_BIT, display lists and deletion. WineD3D then reports the GeForce FX 5800's TextureCaps, POW2|NONPOW2CONDITIONAL (D3D9 0x7ed87, D3D8 0x7ed9f from 0x7ec87/0x7ec9f); Wine 0049 keeps formats a rectangle cannot hold (DXTn, depth) in padded 2D textures and unpads only rectangles, so NPOT render targets, backbuffers, offscreen surfaces and textures are exact-size rectangles while NPOT DXT textures still fail (D3DERR_NOTAVAILABLE) and mipmapped NPOT textures D3DERR_INVALIDCALL. The installed D3D8/9 NPOT probe, macOS CGL (its IOSurface export binds a native rectangle texture), Win98/XP guests and games remain to be run.

contracts.api: OpenGL 1.1 + ARB_depth_texture, ARB_shadow and ARB_fragment_program_shadow (D3D8/D3D9 D16/D24X8/D24S8 shadow-map textures through Wine)
contracts.operation: second capability word negotiation; depth image definition/subimage/copy from the depth buffer/readback, zero-defined storage, proxies, framebuffer attachment, compare mode/function and depth texture mode with their errors, comparison sampling (NEAREST, LINEAR, projective) in fixed function and SHADOW1D/2D/RECT programs, display lists
contracts.format: DEPTH_COMPONENT(16/24/32), DEPTH_STENCIL and DEPTH24_STENCIL8 without a border; DEPTH_COMPONENT pixels of every scalar type, packed UNSIGNED_INT_24_8
contracts.usage: shadow maps: render depth, sample with comparison
contracts.remaining: Negotiated by DG_CAP2_GL_DEPTH_TEXTURE, the first bit of the second capability word DG_GL_REG_CAPS2 (0x1194), which older hosts read as zero and kernels report in the CAPABILITIES reply's DeviceError (zero from older kernels); without it every new name keeps its GL_INVALID_ENUM and depth images stay EXT_packed_depth_stencil's TEXTURE_2D ones. No new records: depth images of 1D, 2D and rectangle targets use the existing records, cube and 3D depth images are local GL_INVALID_OPERATION, compare/mode values beyond ARB_shadow and ARB_depth_texture (no EXT_shadow_funcs) local GL_INVALID_ENUM, and GetTexImage level-word bit DG_GL_TEXTURE_READ_DEPTH reads float depth or, with READ_FLOAT, packed words after the frontend checked the level's depth and stencil sizes. Native pixel tests (Linux, private Mesa on Radeon) pass; Mesa's fixed-function 1D lookups compare t instead of r. WineD3D then accepts D16, D24X8 and D24S8 as depth textures (D3DERR_NOTAVAILABLE before); Wine 0050 refuses D16_LOCKABLE, D32, INTZ and depth cube/volume textures as a GeForce FX did, and makes NPOT D16/D24X8/D24S8 depth-stencil surfaces exact-size rectangles; Wine 0051 names SHADOW targets in the arbfp fixed-function replacement and ARB pixel shaders. The installed D3D8/9 depth texture probe, macOS CGL, Win98/XP guests and games remain to be run.

contracts.api: OpenGL 1.1 internal format RGB565 without an extension name (D3D8/D3D9 R5G6B5 textures, render targets and 16-bit back buffers through Wine)
contracts.operation: second capability word negotiation; RGB565 image definition/subimage/proxy/copy from the framebuffer/readback, framebuffer attachment and renderbuffer storage, display lists
contracts.format: RGB565 (0x8D62) internal format; every pixel format and type of the colour images
contracts.resource: 1D, 2D, rectangle, cube face and 3D colour texture; renderbuffer
contracts.usage: 16-bit colour textures and render targets with six green bits
contracts.remaining: Negotiated by DG_CAP2_GL_RGB565, the second bit of DG_GL_REG_CAPS2; without it RGB565 keeps the local error of any unknown internal format. No extension name and no ARB_ES2_compatibility entry point: WineD3D's GL_RGB565 entry for B5G6R5 needs ARB_ES2_compatibility, so Wine 0057 asks the frontend directly (a 1x1 RGB565 texture, then GetError) and otherwise keeps GL_RGB5, which Mesa stores in 5/5/5 bits (a 6-bit green 13 read back as 12). The host stores RGB565 natively where the native GL has it (GL 4.1 or ARB_ES2_compatibility; Mesa on Linux) and in RGB8 elsewhere (macOS legacy CGL, unverified), exact for every 5/6/5 value in either. Native pixel tests (Linux, Mesa on Radeon) round-trip all 65536 words and check clears, a texture sampled 1:1, DrawPixels, CopyTexImage/CopyTexSubImage and a renderbuffer exactly. X1R5G5B5 (RGB5), A1R5G5B5 (RGB5_A1) and A4R4G4B4 (RGBA4) were already exact on Mesa and are unchanged; color-keyed R5G6B5 textures are still converted to B5G5R5A1 by Wine (five green bits). contracts.api: OpenGL 1.2 core: GL_VERSION, SGIS_texture_lod LOD clamps, EXT_rescale_normal and EXT_draw_range_elements (Homeworld 2's GL renderer and other titles that gate on the version)
contracts.operation: second capability word negotiation; GL_VERSION 1.2 only with every GL 1.2 feature negotiated; TEXTURE_MIN_LOD/MAX_LOD TexParameter and GetTexParameter; RESCALE_NORMAL IsEnabled/Get; MAX_ELEMENTS_VERTICES/INDICES; DrawRangeElements
contracts.resource: 1D, 2D, cube map, 3D and rectangle texture parameters; client-array and buffer element draws
contracts.usage: applications that require GL 1.2 by version
contracts.remaining: Negotiated by DG_CAP2_GL_CORE_1_2, the fourth bit of DG_GL_REG_CAPS2. GL_VERSION is 1.2 only with it, DG_CAP_GL_TEXTURE_3D, DG_CAP_GL_FIXED_STATE (edge clamp) and secondary colour (separate specular colour); BGRA and every packed pixel type were already accepted. Without the bit the LOD names stay a local GL_INVALID_ENUM and the version 1.1. DrawRangeElements is a DrawElements (every draw bounds its own indices) under its core name only; no extension name changes, and WineD3D's version promotions add only EXT_texture3D, which the same capability already advertised. Homeworld 2 (demo 0.99) refuses 1.1 outright: GL.dll parses "1.1" with x87 double arithmetic and compares it below the float 1.1f, then exits with code 0 and no message; with 1.2 (Win2000, package m55 on Linux/Mesa) it shows a dismissable 'plays best with OpenGL 1.3' notice, then the menu (about 330 FPS) and the first mission (about 110-130 FPS). Native tests (Linux, Mesa) check the CAPS2 bit, MIN/MAX_LOD records and queries and the level a minified draw samples under each clamp, RESCALE_NORMAL through IsEnabled and the MAX_ELEMENTS hints. macOS CGL, Win98/XP guests and the imaging subset (not claimed: no ARB_imaging) remain.

contracts.api: OpenGL 1.1 GetTexImage, GetCompressedTexImage and ReadPixels (WineD3D whole-surface locks, GetFrontBuffer and CPU blit fallbacks)
contracts.operation: second capability word negotiation; one-query level shape; unit-counted texture reads and ReadPixels of up to 4 MiB per QUERY through a kernel-owned page list
contracts.format: RGBA8/BGRA, RGB565, float RGBA, depth, packed depth-stencil, stencil, S3TC
contracts.resource: texture level (1D, 2D, rectangle, cube face, 3D), window and framebuffer object
contracts.remaining: Negotiated by DG_CAP2_GL_BULK_READ, the third bit of DG_GL_REG_CAPS2. A QUERY result above 64 KiB goes through a page list (DG_GL_RESULT_PAGES): NT and Win9x kernels keep a 4 MiB buffer and its frame list in driver memory for the adapter's life; the device checks the list and its pages as writable RAM at submission and before writing and never writes outside them. Shape (one query) plus one 3 MiB read replace 3 GetTexLevelParameteriv and 48 GetTexImage round trips for a 1024x768 RGBA8 level (Warcraft III locks its back buffer read-only every present); a 1024x768 ReadPixels is one query instead of 48. Results are byte-identical to the chunked reads older hosts, kernels and frontends keep. Native tests (Linux, Mesa on Radeon) cover RGBA8, BGRA uploads, RGB565, depth, packed depth-stencil, float, S3TC, window colour/depth/stencil/float reads on both transports and malformed lists. The installed probe's 1024x768 whole-surface stage, Win98/XP/2000 guests, macOS CGL and Warcraft III FPS remain to be run.

contracts.api: D3D8/D3D9/DirectDraw (WineD3D, USE_WIN32_OPENGL) over the DreamGPU WGL frontend
contracts.operation: per-operation context acquisition: the pixel format of WineD3D's own GetDC window DC verified or set once per context and window, not queried (wglGetPixelFormat, a WindowFromDC system call on NT) on every first-level acquire
contracts.remaining: Far Cry (D3D9, about 200 FPS) is guest-CPU-bound with about 17% of guest time in the NT kernel, much of it system calls on WineD3D's per-operation path. The native context owner is released after every operation (deliberately, for cross-thread handoff), so every acquisition re-activated the context and asked the frontend for the window's pixel format. Wine patch 0063 keeps hdc_has_format for a window DC, as Wine did for private DCs, once the context's format was verified or set on it: steady state makes no wglGetPixelFormat call. It is verified again after the swapchain's window changes, after a failed binding, and on a new context (reset); a window with another format, a class DC (CS_CLASSDC) or WGL_WINE_pixel_format_passthrough (restore_pf) is checked on every acquisition as before. Source test: the prepared acquire/release/activation/pixel-format functions against a window/DC model (9 mutations rejected). The guest CPU profile of Far Cry remains to be measured; wglMakeCurrent itself still looks the window up (WindowFromDC, GetClientRect) on every acquisition.

contracts.api: OpenGL 1.1 client arrays + EXT_compiled_vertex_array (Quake III-engine renderers, WineD3D user-memory draws)
contracts.operation: DrawElements of client arrays as one buffer draw without buffer slots (each array's indexed range once, inline indices); LockArraysEXT/UnlockArraysEXT and the lock queries as client state; ArrayElement records
contracts.format: every client array descriptor; UNSIGNED_BYTE/SHORT/INT indices
contracts.remaining: Negotiated by DG_CAP_GL_VERTEX_BUFFER_OBJECT; without it EXT_compiled_vertex_array stays hidden and every indexed client draw keeps its per-index expansion. With it an indexed draw of client arrays alone is the existing buffer draw with a zero buffer mask whenever that is no larger than the expansion and fits one packet; the host bounds every inline index by the client vertices at admission. Sparse or oversized ranges, display list compilation and errors keep the expansion. The lock is client state only (saved by CLIENT_VERTEX_ARRAY_BIT, never recorded); locked draws submit the unlocked records, so the host retains nothing between draws. Native pixel tests show identical images for both records; the Quake III timedemo, guest CPU profile, Win98/XP guests and macOS CGL remain to be measured.
